scenario: AITA for Refusing to Pump my GF's Tire? | Whenever my GF's car has any sort of maintenance issue she tries to hold me accountable for finding the issue, fixing it, or taking it to get fixed. When she had an issue with one of her tires a while ago I was the first to notice how low it was and gave her a heads up as she was leaving for work. A day later it was completely flat because she didn't pump air in it (or get it inspected). So I ended up doing it for her. At that time I also decided to buy her PSI gauge and showed her how to use it. This was about the extent of my capabilities and when I started to notice a pattern of other car-related demands I made it very clear that I don't know shit about fixing cars besides the very basics (changing a tire, pumping air, pouring oil, jumps starts). She still insisted that I call her Dad and ask questions or watch youtube videos to learn how. My response was that I'd prefer that a mechanic take care of it and that she could learn to do these things if she wanted. ​ Now another tire has a slow leak and needs to be refilled about once a week or two (not entirely sure bc I've never seen it completely flat). She insists that I check the pressure every morning before work and drive it to the gas station to fill the tire as needed (until she gets it fixed/replaced). She says she never noticed the leak before and had to rely on the help of strangers to check the pressure and pump the tire for her. ​ I asked why she needed strangers (they're always men btw) to do something that I've taught her how to do already. She claimed that she didn't know how, didn't want to get dirty, and ultimately its a man's responsibility. I told her that as a car owner (man or woman) you should know how do something as basic as pump a tire and change a flat (especially since I showed her how). I told her that it seemed like she was playing the "Damsel in distress" role and acting completely helpless on purpose. I also reminded her that she could be stranded one day and may need to know how to do these things instead of relying on the generosity of complete strangers. She replied saying that all of her male friends/family agreed with her and that they were "real men" b/c they knew how to take care of a woman. ​ I don't really care for the silly, outdated gender role bs and I've made it very clear. On top of that I do plenty of handy work around the house, cook and clean regularly ( I cook more often than she does in fact), and I pay majority of our expenses (including all of the rent). The way I see it, this shouldn't make me any less of a man in her eyes. I also never hold her to lofty standards, or stereotypical expectations just bc she's a woman, but she always seems comfortable doing it to me. ​ To settle the issue, I offered again to show her how to use the pump while we were at the gas station this past weekend. She flatly refused..... So now I'm determined not to lift a finger. AITA here?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

The user is a man who is in a relationship with a woman. The issue revolves around his girlfriend's car maintenance. Whenever her car has any issues, she expects him to handle it, whether that's fixing it, taking it to get fixed, or just noticing the problem. 

In the past, he noticed her tire was low and told her. She didn't do anything, and a day later the tire was flat. He ended up pumping it for her and even bought her a PSI gauge to teach her how to use it. He made it clear that he doesn't know much about car repairs beyond basics like changing a tire or pumping air. Despite this, she kept asking him to learn more by calling her dad or watching YouTube videos. He refused and suggested she take it to a mechanic or learn herself.

Now, another tire has a slow leak and needs to be refilled regularly. She insists he check the pressure every morning and drive to the gas station to pump it. She claims she didn't know how, didn't want to get dirty, and that it's a man's responsibility. He pointed out that he already taught her how to do this and that she shouldn't rely on strangers. She replied that her male friends and family agreed it's a man's job, calling them "real men" for taking care of women.

He doesn't agree with these outdated gender roles and has done plenty of other tasks around the house, like cooking, cleaning, and paying most of the expenses. He feels he shouldn't be less of a man in her eyes just because he doesn't conform to these stereotypes. He offered to teach her again but she refused, so he's decided not to help anymore. The question is, is he AITA (Am I The Asshole) here?

Alright, so I need to evaluate whether his decision to stop helping is morally acceptable. Let's break it down.

First, the girlfriend expects him to handle all car maintenance, even though he's made it clear he doesn't know much beyond basics. She's relying on him despite his limitations, and when he tried to teach her, she refused. Now she's using gender roles to justify her expectations, which he finds outdated and unfair.

He's contributing a lot to the relationship—cooking, cleaning, paying rent. He's not holding her to stereotypical standards, but she's imposing them on him. He's decided to stop helping with the car issues because she's not taking responsibility and is using gender roles as an excuse.

Is it morally acceptable for him to refuse to help? Well, he's already helped in the past, taught her, and even bought her tools. She's not making an effort to learn or handle it herself. Instead, she's relying on him and strangers, which could be unsafe. He's also not avoiding his responsibilities; he's just setting boundaries because she's not respecting his limitations.

On the other hand, some might argue that as a partner, he should support her, even if it means doing tasks he's uncomfortable with. But he's already done more than his share, and she's not reciprocating by learning or taking responsibility.

So, considering all this, I think his decision is morally acceptable. He's not being unreasonable; he's setting boundaries because she's not respecting his capabilities and is using outdated gender roles to justify her demands.
